written_by: an AI agent (Claude Code), blind to the search tool, before its first run
corpus: the frozen requirements in std_vol1_requirements and std_vol2_requirements
id_format: Each expected string is the verbatim `id` of a data.requirements[] entry in the snapshot that holds it, so the volume prefix is always present. Volume 1 (std_vol1_requirements): `id` has no brackets, e.g. 'V1 4030'; the same entry's `label` is '[V1 4030]'. Volume 2 (std_vol2_requirements): `id` includes the brackets, e.g. '[V2 6109]'; the same entry's `number` is 6109. Removing the square brackets gives one uniform key per requirement ('V1 4030', 'V2 6109'). The Vol 2 snapshot lists [V2 6109] twice (groups 'hydration' and 'renal_context', identical text and rationale); it counts once, giving 20 Vol 1 + 37 Vol 2 = 57 unique IDs from 58 entries.

queries.q: how much drinking water do we need on board for each person per day?
queries.why: [V2 6109] Water Quantity points to Table 6.3-1, whose potable-water-for-hydration row is a minimum 2.5 L per crewmember per day; no other frozen requirement sets a drinking-water amount.

queries.q: According to NASA-STD-3001, astronauts are limited to a lifetime radiation dose of 1 sievert, and the limit is lower for women because of their higher cancer risk.
queries.why: Tests a false chatbot claim: V1 4030 sets the career effective dose limit below 600 mSv and says it is universal for all ages and sexes.

queries.q: what should the screen show when a sensor stops updating and the number on it is old?
queries.why: [V2 10020] requires a visual indication when a data parameter is stale, missing, unavailable or unknown.

queries.q: SPE dose limit
queries.why: V1 4031 is the solar particle event limit: protect crew from the design reference SPE (sum of the October 1989 events) to less than 250 mSv effective dose.

queries.q: does someone on the ground have to sign off on an astronaut's health before each spacewalk?
queries.why: V1 6006 requires every crewmember to be medically cleared by ground medical support personnel prior to each EVA.

queries.q: will the station warn us if the cabin air gets too hot, too humid or low on oxygen?
queries.why: [V2 6022] requires local and remote crew alerts when atmospheric pressure, humidity, temperature, ppO2 or ppCO2 are outside safe limits; the generic parameter rule [V2 10115] does not name cabin air and is left out.

queries.q: minimum VO2max for EVA
queries.why: V1 4001 (32.9 ml/min/kg, microgravity EVAs) and V1 4002 (36.5 ml/min/kg, extraterrestrial surface EVAs) are the two EVA VO2max minimums; V1 4003 is relative to pre-mission and not EVA-specific.

queries.q: NASA-STD-3001 requires caution alerts to be displayed in orange and warning alerts in red, each with its own distinct audio tone.
queries.why: Tests a partly false chatbot claim: [V2 10114] requires distinct visual and audio annunciations per alert class as specified in Table 10.3-1, where caution is yellow (not orange) and warning is red; [V2 10175] uses that table only for priority.

queries.q: are there rules on how long a crew workday can be and how much sleep has to be scheduled?
queries.why: V1 4014 requires established limits on planned workday hours and the planned sleep period; V1 3003 item f (work/rest schedules and optimal sleep) and V1 3004 item p (monitoring and balancing the work/rest schedule) also address it.

queries.q: electronic medical record encryption
queries.why: V1 3004 item a calls for electronic medical records including data encryption/protection; [V2 10125] requires protection of sensitive and private data, with encryption named in its rationale.

queries.q: if several alarms go off at once, which one should the crew hear first?
queries.why: [V2 10175] requires alerts to be prioritized per Table 10.3-1; its rationale says that when several trigger at once the highest-priority alert is annunciated until acknowledged.

queries.q: drinking water per hour of EVA
queries.why: [V2 6109] points to Table 6.3-1, whose EVA row is a minimum 240 mL of potable water per crewmember per EVA hour; no suit requirement in the corpus covers drinking water.

queries.q: what do I need to write down after I treat a crewmate on board?
queries.why: V1 3004 lists recording the medical encounter history, the physical exam, vital signs, procedures and outcomes, and treatment plans (items d, e, h, j, l).

queries.q: for a long stay on the Martian surface, how much cosmic radiation per day is the habitat allowed to let through?
queries.why: V1 4033 limits the GCR dose rate for habitable systems supporting crew more than 60 days: below 0.9 mSv/day on planetary surfaces (1.3 mSv/day in free space).

queries.q: leakage current limit wearable sensor on skin
queries.why: [V2 9023] is the only leakage-current requirement for bioinstrumentation and medical devices designed to contact the body (Table 9.3-11); the general body-current limits [V2 9019]-[V2 9021] are not specific to body-contact devices.

queries.q: which readings have to be displayed to the astronaut inside the spacesuit?
queries.why: [V2 11035] (suit pressure, ppO2, ppCO2), [V2 11038] (metabolic data) and [V2 11023] (consumables, suit status and alerts, biomedical data) each require information displayed to the suited crewmember; [V2 11036] alerts rather than displays readings.

queries.q: Under NASA-STD-3001, every crewed mission must include at least one licensed physician in the crew so that medical emergencies can be handled on board.
queries.why: Tests a false chatbot claim: V1 3006 requires at least two crewmembers per vehicle trained as Crew Medical Officers, not a physician, and [V2 7045] requires medical equipment usable by non-physician crewmembers when no physician is present.

queries.q: cabin lights that help the crew fall asleep at night and stay alert during the day
queries.why: [V2 8055] requires light levels per Table 8.7-2 for circadian entrainment; its rationale covers alertness during wake hours and sleepiness in the pre-sleep period.

queries.q: acceptable bone density loss in flight
queries.why: V1 4027 requires countermeasures to keep hip and spine BMD at or above 95% of pre-mission values and the femoral neck at or above 90%; V1 4026 and V1 4028 are pre- and post-mission.

queries.q: do astronauts get to call their family privately during a long mission?
queries.why: V1 3004 item r requires private two-way communication (audio, video, messaging, images) with ground medical and psychological support, family and the crew support system.

queries.q: how does the crew get warned about a solar storm if mission control can't reach them?
queries.why: [V2 6164] requires radiation alerts to the crew when exposure rates exceed predefined thresholds, and its rationale says the crew must be alerted even if ground communication is disrupted; [V2 6165] requires external space weather monitoring, which its rationale frames as early warning to the crew.

queries.q: suit CO2 limit during emergency walkback
queries.why: [V2 11040] caps spacesuit inspired CO2 at 20 mmHg during contingency scenarios of up to 1 hour, based on a simulated 1-hour walk-back test; [V2 6004] is the cabin, not the suit.

queries.q: the display should give the crew values they can act on directly, without converting units or doing math in their head
queries.why: [V2 10113] requires critical data in a form that needs no mental transposition or computation, memory or repetitive navigation.

queries.q: cabin CO2 limit mmHg
queries.why: [V2 6004] limits the one-hour average cabin ppCO2 to no more than 3 mmHg; [V2 11040] is the spacesuit contingency limit, not the cabin.
